summary: On-demand evidence slab + security questionnaire backfill for EuroBank: signed webhook sample, deletion proof, and event-ownership map
description: Issue summary: EuroBank AG (enterprise customer) needs a compact evidence slab to respond to a regulator Q2 request. They require: 1) A signed sample webhook envelope (per-tenant) using their provided public key; 2) Proof of deletion for three user_ids with RFC3161-style timestamp attestation; 3) An event-ownership mapping (which service produces each audit event and which field contains the tenant identity) and a small date-range SIEM-friendly payload sample (JSON lines, ~1k events) with redaction markers. Impact: Regulatory deadline in 48 hours; customer cannot complete their SOC/Regulator questionnaire without these artifacts. Requested deliverables: signed-webhook-sample.json, deletion-proof-ids.txt (with timestamps and checksums), event-ownership-map.csv, siem-sample-2026-03-01-2026-03-03.ndjson. Business context: EuroBank is undergoing on-site audit next week and needs artifacts for legal/AML review. Contact: legal@eurobank.example and the primary support contact Viktor Petrov. Deadline: end of day 2026-03-14 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer attempted to pull a 3-day sample via Console > Audit exports > On-demand; 2) Export UI returned an 'Export queued' tray but no delivery appeared in S3 / webhook within 30 minutes; 3) Customer attempted the webhook test with their public key and validation failed (signature mismatch); 4) Customer reached out for signed sample and deletion attestation. Attach: screenshot of Console export state, webhook error payload, and sample idempotency token: export-req-52910.
logs: Export job traces: audit-service/job/52910 -> queued at 2026-03-13T09:12:04Z -> dispatched to worker-7 -> worker-7 logged transient 504 to s3-uploader and retried 3x. Webhook delivery log: webhook/send/98721 -> HTTP 200 to customer but signature-sample header absent in delivery (header 'X-Signature' missing). Deletion pipeline: GM-delete/ids/2026-02-24 shows tombstone created, but attestation record not included in public deletion manifest (manifest index 1142).
comments: 2026-03-13T10:02:12Z - Support - Aisha Malik: Opened ticket after phone call with Viktor. Asked SRE to check worker-7 and s3-uploader retries. SLA P1 noted.

2026-03-13T11:05:47Z - SRE - Kevin Brown: Confirmed worker-7 saw intermittent 504s to internal s3 proxy between 09:08-09:15Z. Uploads retried and eventually succeeded; need to verify post-processing step that attaches signature header. Investigating webhook signing component.

2026-03-13T13:24:30Z - Engineering - Priya Shah: Found a regression in webhook-signer where env var SIGNING_KEY_PATH was null in the on-demand export job runner for enterprise exports created via Console. PR to add fallback and test is ready (linked above).

2026-03-14T08:40:05Z - Support - Lena Ortiz: Reached out to customer with ETA for signed sample (3 hours) and asked for their public key and list of user_ids for deletion proof. Provided temporary on-demand download link for raw ndjson sample.

2026-03-14T12:10:00Z - Customer - Viktor Petrov (EuroBank): Uploaded public key (rsa-2048) and confirmed user_ids: 42f7c9, 8a2d11, d5b001. Asked whether RFC3161 attestation will be included in deletion proof.

2026-03-14T14:22:11Z - SRE - Kevin Brown: Delivered provisional deletion manifest signed with our timestamping service; need security to validate that RFC3161 nonce/timehsm format acceptable to EuroBank. Asked secops for confirmation.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: webhook-signer env var null caused header absence for console-initiated exports. Reproducer: create on-demand export via Console and inspect delivery headers for X-Signature.
Observed: uploads eventually succeeded but post-upload signing hook didn't run for console path due to code path regression introduced in PR 787 (missing init in export job).
Workaround: manually run signer for the specific export id and attach signature header to payload; produced a signed-webhook-sample.json for customer validation.

Deletion attestation: backend created tombstones with internal audit id; we can produce an RFC3161-compatible timestamp proof using internal timestamper service timestamper-3 and include SHA256 checksums for each deleted object.

Event-ownership map: compiled map from codebase (audit_emitter module) showing which service emits which event types; normalized tenant field is 'tenant_id' in most events, but some legacy events use 'org_id'—need to mark as legacy in CSV.
resolution: Provided on-demand evidence slab to customer: 1) signed-webhook-sample.json (envelope signed with our signing key and verifiable with customer's RSA pubkey); 2) deletion-proof-2026-03-14.txt containing RFC3161 timestamp tokens from timestamper-3 and SHA256 checksums; 3) event-ownership-map-2026-03-13.csv (with legacy mappings highlighted); 4) siem-sample-2026-03-01_03.ndjson (pseudonymized tenant ids and redaction markers). Engineering deployed a rollback for the webhook-signer regression (PR 821) and a follow-up test added to the export-runner suite. Security confirmed RFC3161 tokens are generated per spec and provided HSM attestation reference. Next steps: close after customer sign-off and add export-runner unit test to prevent regressions.
